subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx latency & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Olivia Price <olivia.price@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T15:04:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — FinEx latency & throughput goals

Hi Alex / Olivia — great to meet today, thanks for walking through the workflow. Quick recap and concrete ask so we can size an appropriate serving topology: 

Recap (from call)
- Primary use case: real-time trade confirmation and short-form explanations returned to traders and compliance. Mostly short prompts + streaming partial responses for progressive UI.
- Model target: open LLM (customer evaluating gpt-3.5-like open models and Llama-variant family).
- Expected quality target: 95% of responses must be crisp within first 300 tokens.

Sizing asks (can you confirm the numbers below or correct?):
1) Typical payload: ~120 input tokens, ~220 output tokens (avg).
2) Expected steady-state QPS: 80 requests/sec.
3) Peak burst QPS: up to 600 QPS for 3–6 minute market events (daily).
4) Concurrency requirement: UI expects p50 partial-stream latency < 200ms; p95 end-to-end generation latency target <= 800ms (non-streaming) and ~500ms for streaming p95.
5) Multitenancy: single tenant (FinEx) but multiple internal teams — will want isolated routes for prod vs staging.
6) Streaming: yes — clients expect chunked tokens as they are generated.

Please confirm the numbers above and attach any traffic samples you have (token histograms, peak windows). If confirmed, we will run a quick capacity estimate and propose a Dedicated baseline + burst plan.

Attachments: traffic_snapshot_Q2.csv (you mentioned this on the call), p0_prompt_samples.txt

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm traffic numbers and attach token histogram if available.
- Redwood: will run throughput calc and propose a baseline config (Dedicated pools + burst).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — good summary. Confirmed numbers (see attached CSV). Highlights: 
- Average tokens per request: input 110–130, output 200–260 (mean ~220).
- Steady-state QPS: 70–90 (varies by hour), we typically see 80 in trading hours.
- Peak events: up to ~580–620 QPS lasting ~4–7 minutes (rare but expected during market opens/earnings).
- Concurrency: we currently have ~150 concurrent user sessions during peak, but each session issues 1–5 parallel requests depending on UI flows.
- Streaming: yes, we need partial tokens streamed to the UI. p50 partial chunk arrival within 150–250ms is ideal; p95 end-to-end completion <= 700ms if possible.

Attached: traffic_snapshot_Q2.csv, p0_prompt_samples.txt

Let us know if you need raw nginx logs vs aggregated histograms.

— Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-24T18:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — FinEx latency & throughput goals

Marissa — forwarding FinEx numbers from Alex. Key points for sizing: avg tokens/request ~220 output, steady 80 QPS, peak ~600 QPS for 4–7m bursts, streaming required with tight p95 targets (~500–700ms).

Quick ask: can you run a ballpark throughput calc (tokens/sec, GPUs required) and recommend a baseline Dedicated configuration we can propose? Items to consider:
- Model: assume quantized 7B Llama variant baseline (we can propose 7B quantized + a fallback 13B for edge cases).
- Target SLOs: p50 partial chunk < 200ms, p95 end-to-end <= 700ms.
- Workload mix: 90% short-form (<= 300 tokens), 10% long-form (500–1000 tokens) — those will be less frequent but impact KV cache utilization.
- Burst handling: want automated burst to cloud GPUs for market events; propose reserved Dedicated baseline for steady traffic and autoscale/burst to additional nodes for peaks.

I added the HubSpot deal (DEAL-9876) and their Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sizing-docs

Can you also draft two options: (A) cost-optimized baseline (assume some relaxed p95) and (B) performance-first baseline to hit p95 targets with headroom for bursts.

Thanks — Rafael

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Olivia Price <olivia.price@finex.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T18:12:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — FinEx latency & throughput goals (sizing options)

Thanks for the numbers, Alex — helpful. High-level sizing notes (ballpark, assumes optimized quantized 7B runtime and streaming enabled):

Quick math / assumptions:
- Avg tokens/request (include input+output): ~330 tokens (110 in + 220 out).
- Steady-state QPS: 80 req/sec => tokens/sec = 80 * 330 = 26,400 tokens/sec.
- Peak QPS: 600 req/sec burst => tokens/sec = 600 * 330 = 198,000 tokens/sec (for 4–7 minutes).
- Effective concurrency during peak (assuming avg generation time ~300ms): ~600 * 0.3 = 180 concurrent generations.

Option A — cost-optimized baseline:
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-class GPUs (quantized 7B) sized for steady-state with token cache + batching. Expected steady throughput ~30k tokens/sec with p95 ~700–900ms (good for steady 80 QPS).
- Burst: autoscale to add 12x A100 for short windows (total 16 GPUs) to handle peaks — will meet peak tokens/sec but may have higher cold-start latency on autoscale.
- Notes: lower monthly cost, acceptable if FinEx can tolerate slightly higher p95 during rare peaks.

Option B — performance-first baseline:
- Dedicated pool: 12x A100-class GPUs reserved to provide headroom. With optimized kernel paths and continuous batching, expect sustained ~120k tokens/sec and p95 ~450–600ms for most requests.
- Burst: autoscale additional 12 GPUs for peaks (total 24) to hit ~240k tokens/sec for the 600 QPS bursts.
- Notes: higher committed cost but better headroom and lower risk of p95 regressions during bursts; recommended if SLAs matter.

Streaming notes:
- We recommend fine-grained streaming support (chunk size ~16–32 tokens) and smaller batch windows for low-latency partial chunks. That reduces p50 partial latency to ~150–250ms in our tests.

Next steps:
- Rafael: propose these two options in the commercial proposal and surface any SLA/commit differences.
- Alex: confirm if FinEx has strict monthly budget constraints or prefers performance-first.
- If both agree, schedule a short technical sizing call (30 min) to validate burst strategy and autoscale behavior.

Attachments: none in this message (we referenced traffic_snapshot_Q2.csv earlier).

— Marissa
